text:
Suppose $h(n) = m$, i.e., $f(g(n)) = m$.  Let $k = g(n)$. Then
 egin{align*}
  \Th{Q} & \Proves !A_g(
um{n}, 
um{k})
  \intertext{since $!A_g$ represents~$g$, and}
  \Th{Q} & \Proves !A_f(
um{k}, 
um{m})
  \intertext{since $!A_f$ represents~$f$. Thus,}
  \Th{Q} & \Proves !A_g(
um{n}, 
um{k}) \land !A_f(
um{k}, 
um{m})
  \intertext{and consequently also}
  \Th{Q} & \Proves \lexists[y][(!A_g(
um{n}, y) \land !A_f(y, 
um{m}))],
\end{align*}
i.e., $\Th{Q} \Proves !A_h(
um{n}, 
um{m})$.
